newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cyclone shuts Australia's Griffin oil rig.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cyclone shuts Australia's Griffin oil rig.

text.p: The Griffin floating oil platform expects to resume production at a rate of around 70,000 barrels a day on Friday, January 3, after disconnecting from its riser on Monday to avoid the path of a cyclone that has since passed, a spokesman for the rig said on Tuesday.

Production from the platform was shut in on Sunday in anticipation of cyclone Phil, which tore through parts of offshore Western Australia earlier this week causing output at a number of fields to cease.
The cyclone has since dissipated and no longer poses a threat to coastal communites, the Bureau of Meteorolgy said.
"We'll probably reconnect on Friday," the spokesman told Reuters.
The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd holds 45 percent of Griffin and is the operator. Mobil Corp holds 35 percent and Inpex Alpha Ltd owns the remaining 20 percent.
The Wandoo oil field offshore of Western Australia was forced to shut-in production of 10,000 barrels a day on Sunday.
Wandoo has recoverable reserves of about 75 million barrels and is operated by Mobil Corp unit, Ampolex Ltd.
Also, the operator of the 90,000-barrel-a-day Cossack-Pioneer oil platform, Woodside Petroleum Ltd, confirmed it had stopped production on Monday to avoid the cyclone.
